scenario: A rare-disease research centre admits clinical fellows who possess advanced biochemical pathway knowledge OR demonstrated patient-advocacy experience. The competencies are independent in the applicant pool; OR-gate admission induces negative within-cohort correlation.

data.description: Population base rates and OR-gate selection mechanism

values.selection_rule: OR gate: selected if (biochemical pathway knowledge) OR (patient-advocacy experience)

question: (a) Derive P(selected) from the OR-gate model. (b) Compute P(biochemistry | ¬patient_advocacy, selected) and explain why it equals 1. (c) Compute P(biochemistry | patient_advocacy, selected) and show it equals P(biochemistry). (d) Quantify the induced conditional correlation direction and explain why it is a selection artefact rather than a genuine population relationship between biochemical pathway knowledge and patient-advocacy experience.

ground_truth.explanation: Under OR-gate selection a candidate who lacks patient-advocacy experience must possess biochemical pathway knowledge to be admitted — hence P(biochemistry|¬patient_advocacy,sel)=1.0. A candidate who already has patient-advocacy experience is admitted regardless of biochemical pathway knowledge, so P(biochemistry|patient_advocacy,sel)=P(biochemistry)=0.4. The gap (1.0 vs 0.4) creates a negative within-selected correlation that is purely a collider-selection artefact.

naive_answer: The negative correlation between biochemical pathway knowledge and patient-advocacy experience observed among selected candidates reflects a genuine trade-off between these traits in the domain.
naive_trap: The negative correlation is entirely a Berkson collider artefact produced by the OR-gate admission rule; the two traits are independent in the full population.
reasoning_trace: (1) P(sel)=P(A)+P(B)-P(A)P(B)=0.4+0.5-0.4×0.5=0.7. (2) Among candidates without patient-advocacy experience: only those with biochemical pathway knowledge are selected → P(biochemistry|¬patient_advocacy,sel)=1.0. (3) Among candidates with patient-advocacy experience: selected regardless of biochemical pathway knowledge → P(biochemistry|patient_advocacy,sel)=P(biochemistry)=0.4. (4) Within-selected: knowing ¬patient_advocacy raises P(biochemistry) from 0.4 to 1.0 → negative conditional correlation despite population independence.
python_verification:
pA,pB = 0.4,0.5
pSel = pA+pB-pA*pB
assert abs(pSel-0.7)<0.005, f'pSel={pSel}'
pA_notB_sel = pA*(1-pB)/(pA*(1-pB))   # =1.0 by definition
assert abs(pA_notB_sel-1.0)<1e-9
pA_B_sel = pA*pB/pB                    # =pA by definition
assert abs(pA_B_sel-0.4)<1e-9
assert pA_notB_sel > pA_B_sel, 'negative collider correlation confirmed'
